history.content: Reviewed PR #1292. The fix skips Python venv directories when scanning skills, inside `loadSkillsFromDirInternal` in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/skills.ts`. It is correct but hand-rolls its own directory skips. A `packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` is still required before merge.
don't we already have infra in other loaders that use the ignore package? shouldn't we be using that here as ewll?

We do have ignore-based infrastructure, but it lives in the package resource discovery in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts` (for example `collectSkillEntries` and `collectAutoSkillEntries`). That path applies `.gitignore`, `.ignore` and `.fdignore` rules through the `ignore` package. The skill loader in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/skills.ts` is separate: it walks the filesystem directly and only skips dotfiles and `node_modules`.
why do we have the skill loader in skills.ts still if package-manager is now responsible for resolving skills? do we still call that?

Yes, we still call it. The package manager only resolves resource paths and metadata; the actual loading, validation and parsing of skill files still happens in `skills.ts`. The call path is `DefaultPackageManager.resolve()` collecting skill paths, then `ResourceLoader.updateSkillsFromPaths()` calling `loadSkills()` in `skills.ts`, and `loadSkillsFromDirInternal()` is still used for default skill directories and for any skill path that is a directory. The package manager does not parse skill content, it only discovers paths.
